```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(janitor)
library(DataExplorer)
```

```{r}
ordway_all <- read_csv("../data/raw/Ordway_weather_water_data_2009_2016.csv")
```

```{r}
# preliminary cleaning
ordway_all <- clean_names(ordway_all)

ordway_all <- ordway_all |>
  select(!year_7) |> 
  mutate(date = mdy(date),
         am_pm = fct(am_pm),
         month = fct(as.character(month)),
         day = fct(as.character(day)),
         year = fct(as.character(year_4)))

```

```{r}
# get basic info
introduce(ordway_all)

plot_intro(ordway_all)
```

There are a significant amount of missing observations; however, no columns are fully missing. About 70% of the variables are continous, and about 30% are discrete. Including the "Notes" variable likely makes it that there are no complete rows, as seen below. It seems reasonable to drop it in the cleaned dataset.

```{r}
# look into missing data
plot_missing(ordway_all)
profile_missing(ordway_all)
```

There is no missing date-related data. Over half of the observations have missing data for water station variables, so we may need to use only a subset of our data when we consider water quality data. There is relatively little missing data for the weather variables, but avag rain duration and avg max windspeed have a higher percentage of missing variables.
